rules.sentence: A history of injury, fever, ulceration, or purulence with acute digit contracture or pain upon flexion/extension would suggest an infectious etiology, whereas a history of longstanding arthritis or autoimmune disorder with slowly progressing symptoms would suggest a chronic systemic process.
These signs are 91 to 97% sensitive for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, however, with a reduced specificity of 51 to 69%.

In rheumatoid arthritis, rheumatoid nodules or hand deformities may be helpful, while crystalline causes can sometimes be elucidated based on the finding of tophi or evidence of deposition on the exam.
A detailed history focusing on possible etiologies is essential, as the cause actively directs treatment of tenosynovitis.
